package_info.package_name: N/A (RepoJacking vulnerability affects any package using renamed GitHub usernames)
package_info.package_manager: Go, Swift, Packagist (and any manager using GitHub URLs as source)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using vulnerable repository URLs (over 10,000 identified)
package_info.why_malicious: This vulnerability enables attackers to hijack the namespace of popular repositories after a GitHub username is renamed. By recreating the original repository under the old username, attackers can serve malicious code to users and automated systems that fetch dependencies from the original repository URL, resulting in widespread supply chain compromise and arbitrary code execution.

execution_context.trigger: repository hijack (namespace takeover after username rename and repository recreation)
execution_context.file_location: N/A (attacker-controlled repository at hijacked namespace, e.g., github.com/olduser/repo)
required_permissions: ability to register the old username
ability to create a repository under the reclaimed username
ability to upload and manage repository content

malicious_snippets.code_language: any (depends on original repository language, e.g., Go, PHP, Swift, JavaScript, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user or package manager fetches or installs from the hijacked repository URL, the attacker's code is downloaded and executed or included in the build process, resulting in arbitrary code execution or supply chain compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Recreation of a previously retired repository namespace by a new owner, especially when the codebase is replaced with attacker-controlled content, is a strong indicator of a supply chain attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users and automated systems expect the repository URL to always resolve to the original, trusted codebase. Instead, it now resolves to untrusted, attacker-controlled code, breaking the trust model of dependency management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repository transfers or username renames may occur, but do not involve recreating a repository with the intent to deceive or serve malicious payloads.
key_indicators: A repository at a previously retired namespace is recreated by a different owner
Drastic changes in repository content or codebase immediately after namespace is reclaimed
Sequence of username rename followed by repository recreation at the old namespace
High-profile or high-download-count repositories suddenly reappear with new, unverified code

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers the old GitHub username after it becomes available due to a username rename by the original owner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to create a repository with the same name as the original popular project under the reclaimed username.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a repository with the same name as the original under the reclaimed username, matching the original repository URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository URL now points to the attacker's repository, breaking the redirect and routing all traffic to attacker-controlled code.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads malicious code to the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users and package managers fetching from the original URL now receive and execute attacker-controlled code, enabling arbitrary code execution or supply chain compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Recreation of a repository at a previously retired namespace by a new owner
Sudden and significant change in repository ownership and codebase at a popular namespace
Sequence of repository transfer, username rename, and subsequent repository recreation at the old namespace
file_indicators: Repository content at a namespace with a history of high clone or download counts that has been recently recreated
Drastic codebase changes (e.g., complete replacement of files or commit history) in a short time window after namespace is reclaimed
network_indicators: Package manager or CI/CD requests to GitHub repository URLs that have recently changed ownership or been recreated
Automated build systems pulling dependencies from GitHub repositories with recent namespace or ownership changes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for recreation of repositories at previously retired or high-profile namespaces, especially following a username rename. Alert on sudden changes in repository ownership or codebase for popular projects. Track package manager and CI/CD fetches from GitHub URLs that have recently changed ownership or content. Use tools to verify the integrity and provenance of dependencies, and enforce the use of immutable references (commit hashes or release tags) instead of mutable URLs. Implement automated alerts for repository recreation events and codebase replacements at known high-risk namespaces.
